alfatah.notes: Uses backend/scraper/alfatah_scraper.py — reads the Shopify analytics JSON embedded in each category page. Set enabled to false to turn this off.

imtiaz.notes: Blink-platform search API for Imtiaz's online store (branch rest_brId=54943). Confirmed working via manual browser testing on 2026-07-27 — returned real product/price data for 'milk'. Prices reflect this specific branch only, not necessarily all Imtiaz locations nationwide. Matching logic in generic_json_scraper.py is basic (substring match on product name) — may pick unrelated products (e.g. 'Milk Chews' candy, baby formula) for broad search terms. Worth spot-checking a few more products before trusting broadly.

naheed.notes: Reads schema.org Product JSON-LD that Naheed embeds for Google SEO (see jsonld_scraper.py). Best-effort: Naheed's product grid itself is drawn by JavaScript, so this only works if their search page also embeds JSON-LD in the initial HTML. If it returns nothing, the app still shows Naheed's manual price from prices.json — this scraper never breaks anything, it just adds a 'Naheed (live)' entry when it succeeds. Set enabled to false to turn it off entirely.

metro.notes: Same JSON-LD technique as Naheed. Metro's site is a Next.js app whose product grid is rendered client-side, so this is the most speculative of the three live scrapers — it depends on whether Metro's server-rendered <head> includes Product schema for SEO. If not, use HOW_TO_FIND_APIS.md to find Metro's real search API and either add a 'type: generic' entry below or ask for a dedicated scraper. Either way, the app falls back to Metro's manual price from prices.json when this returns nothing.
